docs.title: Check one rule
docs.text:
topology-checker <group> <rule> <input> [--layer NAME] [--other INPUT] [--other-layer NAME] [-o OUTPUT]

topology-checker line must-not-have-dangles roads.gpkg --layer roads -o errors.gpkg
topology-checker point must-be-covered-by-lines stops.geojson --other routes.gpkg

Groups are point, line, polygon and geometry. See Rules. Without --layer, each layer in the input is checked separately. Two-layer rules check every input layer against every --other layer.

docs.title: Check a topology definition
docs.text:
tolerance = 0.001

[layers]
roads = { path = "city.gpkg", layer = "roads" }
stops = { path = "stops.geojson" }

[[rules]]
rule = "line/must-not-have-dangles"
layer = "roads"

[[rules]]
rule = "point/must-be-covered-by-lines"
layer = "stops"
other = "roads"

topology-checker validate topology.toml -o errors.gpkg

tolerance and layer are optional. Paths are relative to the TOML file. Unknown keys are errors.

docs.title: Tolerance and CRS
docs.text:
Tolerance is in coordinate units, and calculations are planar. --tolerance overrides the TOML value. If neither is set, the default depends on the CRS:

  • projected CRS: 1 mm;
  • geographic CRS: 1e-8 degrees;
  • unknown CRS, or any input without one: 0.

Inputs must share a CRS; the CLI does not reproject. GeoJSON without a crs member is EPSG:4326. A geographic CRS with a nonzero tolerance prints a warning, because calculations are planar.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text:
-o writes errors_point, errors_line and errors_polygon layers. The format comes from the file extension or from --driver; topology-checker drivers --write lists the formats. Nothing is written when there are no violations. An existing file needs --overwrite.

Columns: violation_id, rule, error_type, origin_layer, origin_fid, origin_part, destination_layer, destination_fid, destination_part. A violation with several geometry types gets a row in each layer, with the same violation_id. Shapefiles shorten the names to viol_id, orig_layer, orig_part, dest_layer, dest_fid and dest_part.

docs.title: Output and exit codes
docs.text:
• stdout: a summary table, or the report as JSON with --json.
  • stderr: warnings, and any error. With --json, an error is printed as {"error": "..."}.
Exit code Meaning 0 No violations 1 Violations found 2 Error

docs.title: Other commands
docs.text:
topology-checker rules                    # add --json for JSON
topology-checker drivers --read --write
topology-checker utilities merge-lines roads.gpkg --layer roads -o merged.gpkg
topology-checker utilities explode-lines roads.gpkg --layer roads -o segments.gpkg

merge-lines joins lines at endpoints shared by exactly two lines. explode-lines splits lines into single segments.

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Requires Rust 1.88 or newer.

cargo install topology-checker --locked

This build reads and writes GeoJSON, GeoPackage, Shapefile, FlatGeobuf, GeoParquet, KML and GPX without GDAL. For other formats, add GDAL:

# Build GDAL from source (needs CMake, a C/C++ compiler and sqlite3)
CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5 cargo install topology-checker --locked --features gdal
# Use an installed GDAL
cargo install topology-checker --locked --features gdal-system

docs.title: Web app
docs.text:
Requires Node.js and Rust 1.88 or newer.

npm ci --prefix web
npm run build --prefix web
cargo build -p topology-checker-web --release --locked

The frontend is embedded in target/release/topology-checker-web. See Web app.

docs.title: Python usage
docs.text: Install from PyPI with uv add topology-checker, or use uv add 'topology-checker[geopandas]' for GeoDataFrame exports and file loading through GeoPandas. Python 3.10 through 3.14 on regular CPython are supported. The base package uses Shapely and pyproj. It does not require GeoPandas or a separate Rust installation when a compatible wheel is available. See the API reference for every class and function.

docs.title: Register and validate
docs.text:
import geopandas as gpd
from topology_checker import Rule, Topology

roads_gdf = gpd.read_file("roads.gpkg")
topology = Topology(tolerance=0.001)
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_NOT_HAVE_DANGLES, roads_gdf)
report = topology.validate()
errors = report.to_geodataframe()
print(report.is_valid, report.error_count, report.warnings)

add_rule accepts a Shapely geometry, a geometry iterable, a GeoSeries, a GeoDataFrame, a GeoJSON mapping, or an object with __geo_interface__. Pass the second layer with the keyword argument other=. Use enum members such as Rule.MUST_NOT_OVERLAP; parse serialized names with Rule("must-not-overlap") before registration.

Each raw input creates a fresh XY snapshot at registration. Later edits to a GeoDataFrame or list do not change that layer. Passing the same raw object to two rules creates two layers, and a generator is consumed on each call. validate() returns an immutable report snapshot; topology violations are results, while invalid registrations raise exceptions and leave the topology unchanged.

docs.title: Reuse a layer explicitly
docs.text:
from shapely.geometry import LineString
from topology_checker import Rule, Topology

topology = Topology(tolerance=0.001)
roads = topology.add_layer(
    [LineString([(0, 0), (1, 0)]), LineString([(1, 0), (2, 0)])],
    name="roads",
    fids=[41, 92],
    crs="EPSG:28992",
)
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_NOT_HAVE_DANGLES, roads)
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, roads)
report = topology.validate()
print(topology.layer(roads).name)
print(report.to_dict())

The returned LayerId belongs to its originating Topology. Reuse it across rules to share the registered layer and native caches. Binary rules require distinct IDs. A RuleSpec returned by add_rule also exposes the registered IDs through .layer and .other.

FIDs default to original input positions, independent of a GeoDataFrame's index or GeoJSON feature IDs. Explicit FIDs must be unique signed 64-bit integers, one per original position, including positions subsequently skipped. Reports preserve FID and multipart provenance in .origin and .destination. Missing and empty features are skipped with warnings, extra dimensions are discarded, and nonfinite retained XY coordinates are rejected. Mixed nonempty families are accepted only by rules with an ANY input signature.

docs.title: Declare ambiguous empty layers
docs.text:
from topology_checker import GeometryKind, Rule, Topology

topology = Topology()
empty_lines = topology.add_layer([], kind=GeometryKind.LINE)
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, empty_lines)
assert topology.validate().is_valid

Family inference uses nonempty parts first, then empty geometry hints. An empty list, only missing values, or conflicting empty hints have no inferred family. Rules with multiple possible signatures then require a declaration through add_layer(..., kind=GeometryKind.POINT), LINE, or POLYGON. A declaration must agree with every retained nonempty part. A uniquely matching rule, such as MUST_NOT_HAVE_DANGLES, can resolve even with unknown empty input.

docs.title: CRS and tolerance
docs.text:
The engine operates in a Cartesian XY plane. It does not reproject, calculate geodesic distances, or infer a CRS from coordinates. Reproject geographic data to an appropriate projected CRS before using distance tolerances.

Tolerance is finite, nonnegative, and expressed in the inputs' coordinate units. For a CRS using metres, 0.001 is one millimetre. It is interpreted by each rule, such as a distance threshold, a minimum retained line length, or a polygon sliver filter. It does not apply a universal geometry buffer or repair geometries. Inspect the concrete rule description for the relevant behavior.

All known layer CRSs must agree. Explicit CRS metadata must agree with metadata on the input. Unknown CRSs are accepted as caller-supplied coordinates. When known and unknown metadata are mixed, validation continues with a warning and the export CRS is unset. Report.to_dict() works without GeoPandas; Report.to_geodataframe() requires the geopandas extra.

docs.title: Geometry-dependent semantics
docs.text:
The 24 public constraints resolve to the 38 concrete rules using the ordered geometry families and whether other= is supplied. These examples illustrate why the concrete variant matters:

Public rule and inputs Meaning MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, points Coincident point pairs within tolerance. MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, lines Shared linework between distinct features; crossings and self-overlaps are excluded. MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, polygons Shared areas between distinct features, excluding slivers below tolerance. MUST_NOT_OVERLAP, lines then polygons Interior or shared boundary line pieces longer than tolerance; isolated contacts are allowed. MUST_BE_INSIDE, points then polygons Strict interior membership; boundary proximity within tolerance is outside. MUST_BE_INSIDE, lines then polygons Pieces outside the polygon union longer than tolerance; boundary linework is covered. MUST_NOT_INTERSECT, lines Overlaps and interior crossings between distinct features; endpoint touches are allowed. MUST_NOT_INTERSECT, lines then polygons Interior pieces, shared boundary pieces and isolated contacts, including boundary proximity within tolerance. MUST_NOT_HAVE_GAPS, polygons Enclosed gaps and an outer-boundary diagnostic; inspect error categories. MUST_NOT_BE_CONTAINED_BY, any then any Whole cleaned features contained by individual targets, excluding mutual containment; no tolerance buffer.

Order matters: line then polygon signatures do not imply polygon then line support. Multipart parts of one feature retain their FID; use the dedicated self-intersection or self-overlap constraints to examine a feature internally.

from shapely.geometry import Point, box
from topology_checker import Rule, Topology

topology = Topology()
topology.add_rule(Rule.MUST_BE_INSIDE, [Point(0.5, 0.5)], other=[box(0, 0, 1, 1)])
result = topology.validate().rules[0]
print(result.resolved_rule.value)
print(result.resolved_rule.description)
for variant in Rule.MUST_NOT_OVERLAP.variants:
    print(variant.inputs, variant.description)

Use .resolved_rule on a RuleSpec, RuleReport, or Violation to inspect the selected semantics. Invalid arity, unsupported families, or ambiguous empty inputs are reported at registration with the supported signatures.

docs.title: Line utilities
docs.text:
from shapely.geometry import LineString
from topology_checker import explode_lines, merge_lines

lines = [LineString([(0, 0), (1, 0)]), LineString([(1, 0), (2, 0)])]
merged = merge_lines(lines, tolerance=0.001)
segments = explode_lines(merged)
assert len(segments) == 2

Both utilities return tuples of Shapely lines. They accept the same input adapters and operate on planar snapshots.

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Run a rule as topology-checker <group> <rule>, or use rule = "<group>/<rule>" in topology.toml. topology-checker <group> <rule> --help prints the exact semantics.

docs.title: Points (10)
docs.text: Rule Needs Description ArcGIS QGIS point/must-not-overlap one point layer Find duplicate points within the distance tolerance. Must Be Disjoint Must not have duplicates point/must-not-overlap-with two point layers Find duplicate points across two layers within the distance tolerance. point/must-be-inside point layer + polygon layer Find points outside the polygons, including points on or within the distance tolerance of their edges. Must Be Properly Inside Polygons Must be inside point/must-be-covered-by-lines point layer + line layer Find points without covering linework, including line endpoints. Must Be Covered By (Point-Line) Must be covered by point/must-be-covered-by-line-endpoints point layer + line layer Find points without a covering open line endpoint. Closed line parts have no endpoints. Must Be Covered By Endpoint Of Must be covered by endpoints of point/must-be-covered-by-polygon-boundaries point layer + polygon layer Find points away from polygon edges, including holes and shared parcel edges. Must Be Covered By Boundary Of (Point-Area) point/must-be-covered-by-polygons point layer + polygon layer Find points outside polygon areas and farther than the tolerance from their edges. Boundary points are allowed. point/must-not-be-inside-polygons point layer + polygon layer Find points strictly inside polygons. Points on or within tolerance of their edges are allowed. point/must-not-intersect-lines point layer + line layer Find points touching linework anywhere, including endpoints, within tolerance. point/must-not-intersect-polygons point layer + polygon layer Find points inside polygons or touching their edges within tolerance.

docs.title: Lines (19)
docs.text: Rule Needs Description ArcGIS QGIS line/must-not-have-dangles one line layer Find unconnected line endpoints. Must Not Have Dangles Must not have dangles line/must-not-have-pseudo-nodes one line layer Find joins connecting exactly two distinct features at their endpoints. Closed loops are allowed. Must Not Have Pseudo Nodes Must not have pseudo nodes line/must-not-overlap one line layer Find shared line segments between distinct features. Crossings and overlaps within one feature are excluded. Must Not Overlap line/must-not-overlap-with two line layers Find shared line segments across two layers. Crossings are excluded. Must Not Overlap With line/must-not-self-overlap one line layer Find line segments traced more than once by the same feature, including across its parts. Must Not Self-Overlap line/must-not-intersect one line layer Find overlaps and crossings between distinct features away from their endpoints. Endpoint touches are allowed. Must Not Intersect line/must-not-intersect-with two line layers Find overlaps and crossings across two layers away from their endpoints. Endpoint touches are allowed. Must Not Intersect With line/must-not-intersect-or-touch-interior one line layer Find overlaps, crossings and endpoint touches on the interior of another feature. Touches only at both features' endpoints are allowed. Must Not Intersect Or Touch Interior line/must-not-intersect-or-touch-interior-with two line layers Find overlaps, crossings and endpoint touches on a line's interior across two layers. Touches only at both features' endpoints are allowed. Must Not Intersect Or Touch Interior With line/must-not-self-intersect one line layer Find overlaps and crossings within one feature. Closed loops and self-touches are allowed. Must Not Self-Intersect line/must-be-inside line layer + polygon layer Find line pieces outside the polygons that are longer than the distance tolerance. Lines on polygon edges are allowed. Must Be Inside line/endpoints-must-be-covered-by-points line layer + point layer Find open line endpoints without a covering point. Closed line parts have no endpoints. Endpoint Must Be Covered By End points must be covered by line/must-be-covered-by-polygon-boundaries line layer + polygon layer Find line pieces that do not follow polygon edges, including holes and shared edges. Must Be Covered By Boundary Of (Line-Area) line/must-not-cross-polygon-boundaries line layer + polygon layer Find lines entering or leaving polygons through exterior or hole edges. Tangencies, endpoint touches and shared segments are allowed. line/must-be-properly-inside-polygons line layer + polygon layer Find whole line parts that leave polygon coverage or come within tolerance of its boundary. line/must-not-overlap-with-polygons line layer + polygon layer Find line pieces inside polygons or along their edges, longer than tolerance. Isolated contacts are allowed. line/must-not-overlap-polygon-boundaries line layer + polygon layer Find line pieces shared with polygon edges, longer than tolerance. Crossings and isolated contacts are allowed. line/must-not-intersect-polygons line layer + polygon layer Find any line contact with polygons, including interior pieces, shared edges and isolated touches within tolerance. line/endpoints-must-be-covered-by-polygon-boundaries line layer + polygon layer Find open line endpoints away from polygon exterior or hole edges. Closed line parts have no endpoints.

docs.title: Polygons (7)
docs.text: Rule Needs Description ArcGIS QGIS polygon/must-not-overlap one polygon layer Find shared areas between distinct polygon features, ignoring slivers below the tolerance. Must Not Overlap Must not overlap polygon/must-not-overlap-with two polygon layers Find shared polygon areas across two layers, ignoring slivers below the tolerance. Must Not Overlap With Must not overlap with polygon/must-not-have-gaps one polygon layer Find enclosed gaps between polygons, ignoring sliver gaps below the tolerance. Also report outer boundaries separately. Must Not Have Gaps Must not have gaps polygon/boundaries-must-be-covered-by-lines polygon layer + line layer Find polygon edge pieces without covering linework, including hole edges. Boundary Must Be Covered By (Area-Line) polygon/must-contain-point polygon layer + point layer Find polygons without a strictly interior point feature. All parts of a point feature must qualify. Contains Point Must contain polygon/must-contain-one-point polygon layer + point layer Find polygons and point features without a one-to-one interior assignment. Count feature IDs, including multipart features. Contains One Point polygon/must-not-contain-points polygon layer + point layer Find strictly contained points, with the polygon as the primary feature. Boundary points are allowed.

docs.title: All geometries (2)
docs.text: Rule Needs Description ArcGIS QGIS geometry/must-not-be-multipart one layer of any geometry type Find features with more than one part. A Multi geometry with only one part is allowed. Must Be Single Part (lines) Must not have multi-part geometries geometry/must-not-be-contained-by two layers of any geometry type Find whole features contained by an individual feature in the other layer. Equal geometries are allowed. No tolerance buffer is used. Check Geometry (Contained)

docs.title: Web app
docs.text:
topology-checker-web                 # http://127.0.0.1:8080
topology-checker-web --port 9000     # or TOPOLOGY_WEB_PORT=9000; 0 picks a free port

Install builds target/release/topology-checker-web. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only and rejects requests with another Host or Origin.

  1. Import a file of up to 512 MiB: GeoJSON, GeoPackage, FlatGeobuf, GeoParquet, KML, KMZ, GPX, or a zipped Shapefile. Or open one of the bundled examples.
  2. Choose layers, a working CRS, a tolerance and rules.
  3. Run the checks, then inspect violations in the table and on the map.
  4. Export violations as one violations layer with the CLI columns. GeoJSON, KML, KMZ and GPX use WGS84. GeoPackage, FlatGeobuf and GeoParquet use the working CRS. A JSON report is also available.
  5. Save a project zip to reopen the setup later.

Each browser tab has its own workspace. Workspaces idle for 4 hours are deleted.
